podcast.body: This song publicly debuted in June 1975 when the Talking Heads opened for The Ramones at CBGB. David Byrne explained on NPR's *Fresh Air* in 2023 that he wrote it as an experiment to combine Alice Cooper's dramatic subject matter with Randy Newman's interior monologue, resulting in an intellectual exploration of violence from "the mind of the killer." The song was later released as part of *Talking Heads: 77* in 1977. "Bern set out to write a song that he thought might be a combination of Alice Cooper like the dramatic subject And Randy Newman like the interior monologue The song might imply violence in the way that punk rock does but this is a bit more intellectual than that We are in the mind of the killer."
